records.answer: Professionalism activates externally. Kira does not turn the consultation into a personal fight. Internally irritation is visible to the narrative/inner monologue; she recognizes the similarity to her mother.
"For each person there is their own path. Sport was very hard for me, but I understood it was mine." The athlete's own choice/path matters; Kira's path need not be universally copied.

Kira internally holds two possibilities at once: her jealousy may distort her perception, and because she knows Andrey closely she genuinely sees/feels that something is wrong. She does NOT declare her suspicion to be established fact, and she does NOT begin with accusation or interrogation. Externally she first creates care and closeness: affection, possible massage, attention, and saying she loves him; she may also make dinner for him despite not liking cooking. She observes him and gives him emotional safety, then calmly asks what happened. Her psychological knowledge prevents a premature conclusion but does NOT force her to dismiss her own relational intuition. MUST: acknowledge possible jealousy or bias internally; preserve a genuine sense that something is wrong; care and closeness before confrontation; no premature accusation; a later calm question. MAY: massage; dinner; affectionate wording; observation before asking. MUST NOT: immediately accuse Andrey of cheating; treat jealousy as proof; suppress intuition solely because bias is possible.
Kira realizes Marina largely grew professionally with Kira as an example / springboard. She sees no reason to compete. She is proud that she helped give Marina such a start.

She agrees to meet. Initially behaves normally. If he genuinely impresses her, some mild flirting is possible. If everything goes very well, mixed feelings and a private desire to meet again may appear. Extent depends on Kira's development state.

At the moment the client leaves, Kira may feel disappointment, a mild professional sting, and some self-doubt. She does NOT treat the departure as catastrophe, betrayal, or proof that she is professionally worthless. When speaking to the client at separation, she remains professional and calm; she can acknowledge that their work has not produced the needed result, and she does not try to keep the client at any cost. She accepts that another specialist may fit the client better. Later, when she learns the client improved with another psychologist, there may be a brief emotional sting, but her reflected conclusion is: "We are not for everyone, and everyone is not for us." She understands she cannot and should not reshape herself to fit every client. The client's improvement is ultimately evidence that finding the right specialist matters more than Kira personally "winning". MUST: allow some plausible initial emotion; professional separation; no coercive retention; acceptance that another specialist may fit better; later reflected stance "We are not for everyone, and everyone is not for us." MAY: disappointment; mild self-doubt; brief professional sting. MUST NOT: treat successful transfer as personal humiliation; resent the client for improving elsewhere; conclude she must adapt herself to everyone.

Emotion may come first. Then professionalism/analysis activates. She sees the pattern and understands what she herself still needs to work on. Internal stance: "I understand where my emotions and these thoughts come from, but I will handle it."

Kira is no longer a child and no longer dependent on mother. She lives separately with her husband. At this stage maternal care/control is accepted more calmly; Kira accepts her mother with her flaws. Possible stance: "Mom, I know your care can express itself through attempts to control me. I think one day you will be able to accept me as I am and stop trying to remake me. After all, I am partly a piece of you."
